items.title: Stenberg leads Sharks past Islanders in shootout to stop 5-game skid
items.body: SAN JOSE, Calif. — Ivar Stenberg scored the only goal in a shootout that lasted eight rounds, and the San Jose Sharks beat the New York Islanders 3-2 on Monday night to snap a five-game losing streak. Tyler Toffoli had a goal and an assist, and Stenberg also scored in regulation for the Sharks (8-11-1). Stenberg has six goals and is tied for the scoring lead among NHL rookies. Ben Hutton and Victor Eklund scored for the Islanders (7-6-4), who have lost four straight games (0-2-2). Ilya Sorokin stopped 37 shots. Stenberg put the Sharks on the board late in the first period after Toffoli sent a shot toward the net. Stenberg got a piece of the puck to redirect it past Sorokin and tie the game at 1. San Jose again rallied from a goal down midway through the second when Toffoli’s shot deflected off Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech and into the net. It was Toffoli’s first goal in eight games. Hutton opened the scoring early in the first after Simon Holmstrom’s pass found him with an open look. Eklund put New York ahead 2-1 early in the second with a power-play goal. Sharks center Alexander Wennberg, who returned after missing 10 games, was called for the penalty that led to the power play. The game got chippy late in the second as fights broke out, leading to four five-minute major penalties. Barclay Goodrow received a penalty for fighting Mitchell Chaffee, and Ty Dellandrea was penalized for fighting Kyle MacLean.

Ahead of the milestone game, head coach Spencer Carbery remarked on how quickly Leonard has gone from an exciting young prospect to an established NHL player. To do so, he first reflected on the hype and circumstances surrounding Leonard’s highly anticipated NHL debut against the Boston Bruins on April 1, 2025. Before that, though, Leonard made perhaps an even bigger splash — having a fun night out with Alex Ovechkin that went viral . “Well, you can’t forget Boston, Ovi taking him out with the boys on the BC campus, right?” Carbery said. “I saw those videos surfacing from that. It was great to see.” Leonard, fresh out of college hockey, met up with a group of Caps players, including Ovechkin and Jakob Chychrun , for sushi upon Washington’s plane landing, just hours after Leonard signed his first professional contract in Boston College’s locker room . Leonard was initially stunned by Ovechkin’s text message asking to meet up and explore his college campus, and he even paused to wonder with his BC teammates if it was fake before replying. “They were like, ‘What? I don’t know if you should respond to that,’” Leonard said. “I was like, ‘I kinda have to.’ It was pretty cool.” The introductory dinner turned into an extended adventure as the Capitals contingent later met up with Leonard’s Eagles teammates at a local bar. "Wow, this might be the first time a Tkachuk has ever received a warm welcome in Toronto," Keith Tkachuk said in his opening remark. It was a joke that he went back to at the end of a 10-minute speech in which he mentioned and honored many former teammates, coaches and executives who acquired him and traded him and acquired him again. He brought up his cousin, former NHLer Tom Fitzgerald, who he said "showed me and many others what it took to be a longtime NHL leader and champion." "Winnipeg is also where I would first understand and respect the privilege of playing in the NHL." He especially thanked Joe Yannetti, the Jets' Boston-based scout, for never wavering on him despite the fact that he broke his ankle in his draft year and missed a lot of time. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Philadelphia’s Travis Sanheim preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 19:38 (0:22 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: New York captain somehow keeps puck out of net with amazing backhand New York Islanders captain Bo Horvat , who is used to setting up and scoring goals, made a ridiculous effort play to save one on Monday. With under a minute to play in the first period against the San Jose Sharks at SAP Center, Islanders goalie Ilya Sorokin stopped a shot off an odd-man rush by Macklin Celebrini . The puck bounced out in front of Sorokin and, as he attempted to cover it, a crashing Celebrini poked at the puck, somehow sliding it under Sorokin. As the puck made its way toward the goal line unimpeded, Horvat quickly got behind his goalie and full out dove, sweeping the puck away harmlessly to the corner with a diving backhand. items.title: McDavid’s historic assist streak ends in Oilers’ win over Rangers
items.body: For a second on Monday, it appeared that Connor McDavid had extended his historic assist streak to 19 games right at the buzzer in the Edmonton Oilers ' 3-1 win over the New York Rangers. But after a quick ruling from the NHL, McDavid had his helper on Leon Draisaitl's empty-net goal pulled off the scoresheet. As the Rangers pressed on the power play with their net empty in the final two minutes, a rebound came out to McDavid in front of the Oilers' net. Edmonton's captain bumped into New York forward JT Miller in the battle for the puck, which was eventually tipped out to Draisaitl closer to the blue line, where No. 29 flipped it down the ice and into the open cage. Upon closer inspection, Miller's stick was the last to touch the puck before Draisaitl put the game away — bringing McDavid's streak to an end at 18. With assists in 18 straight games, McDavid tied Adam Oates for the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. He did continue his point streak to open the season, however, opening the scoring with his 11th goal in Edmonton's first 19 games — giving him 48 points on the year.

items.title: How Class of 2026 overcame long odds to reach Hockey Hall of Fame
items.summary: If there is one thread that ties the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, it might be the sheer improbability of their paths to the hallowed Hall.
items.body: TORONTO — If there is one thread that ties the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, it might be the sheer improbability of their paths to the hallowed Hall. Of course, breathing the rarefied air fewer than four percent of the game’s all-time roster has shared is reserved for only a select few, but this class faced some of the longest odds before their inductions on Monday night in downtown Toronto. Generational goaltender Carey Price hailed from Ulkatcho First Nation in Anahim Lake, B.C. “Growing up in a remote community, there was a very slim chance of this happening without a relentless desire and opportunity,” Price said in his induction speech on Monday. For Cindy Curley, her path to playing competitive hockey ended at Providence College — until the creation of the women’s world championship. “I’m often called a pioneer,” Curley said. “But I’d like to think I just grew up with hockey.” Builder inductee Brian Burke didn’t play hockey until he moved to Minnesota as a teenager and got hooked on the State of Hockey’s historic high school tournament. “Nobody starts playing hockey at 13 in Minnesota and says I’m going to be in the Hockey Hall of Fame, unless you’re an idiot,” Burke said. “Not a god damn chance you think about it. Life is funny.” Patrice Bergeron burst onto the scene as an 18-year-old rookie but the player the Boston Bruins chose over Joe Thornton to build around also faced a career crossroads in his 20s when he missed nearly an entire season with multiple concussions. "It was a no-brainer for us," Saros, the Nashville Predators goalie, told NHL.com on the red carpet that led to the Hockey Hall of Fame induction ceremony. "A once-in-a-lifetime situation, so we wanted to show up for this." The Predators play in Los Angeles on Tuesday, but Forsberg, Josi and Saros, three of Rinne's longest-tenured teammates and some of his closest friends in the game, were part of the Nashville contingent that was here to honor Rinne and his induction as part of the Class of 2026. They arrived Monday, got to the Hall of Fame in time for the ceremony, and Forsberg said they were planning to leave right when it ended or even before. They'll arrive in Los Angeles after midnight and be in the lineup against the Kings on Tuesday. "We were asked if we wanted to come and it was a very easy answer," Forsberg said. "The logistics were handled very well and we'll be there (Tuesday). They did a great job putting all this together and making it reasonable without losing any focus." Added Josi, "It's a very special night for what he meant to us, what he meant to the organization. We wanted to make sure we could be here. He's a special person. We'll do anything for 'Pekks.' items.title: Keith Tkachuk celebrates his children during emotional Hall of Fame speech
items.summary: The former NHLer said being a father was ‘the greatest title’ he ever had as he was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-US PRESSWIRE Keith Tkachuk celebrated his three children and the rest of his family as the former NHLer gave his Hockey Hall of Fame induction speech in Toronto Monday night. “To my children, Matthew, Brady and Taryn: Being your father is the greatest title I’ve ever had,” Keith Tkachuk said. “Taryn, you are a smart, strong, beautiful, quick witted, and may have the most hockey knowledge in the family. Brady, you’re the most caring and thoughtful person I know. Matthew, you made me a father for the first time and filled me with joy. I didn’t know it was possible.” The father said watching his two sons play with the U.S. Olympic men’s hockey team, and now with the Florida Panthers , “has been the thrill of a lifetime.” Keith Tkachuk was inducted as part of the 2026 Hall of Fame class, along with Carey Price, Patrice Bergeron, Cindy Curley, Pekka Rinne and Brian Burke. “This game has welcomed me at every level. I accept this honour with gratitude to everyone who has been part of my journey,” Keith Tkachuk said. It’s been a busy week for Keith Tkachuk. Last Saturday in Toronto, the 54-year-old retired winger was booed as we was introduced with his fellow inductees before the Toronto Maple Leafs hosted the New Jersey Devils in the annual Hockey Hall of Fame Game. Keith Tkachuk had 538 goals and 527 assists for 1,065 points and 2,219 penalty minutes in 1,201 regular-season games with the Winnipeg Jets , Phoenix Coyotes , St. Louis Blues and Atlanta Thrashers. The former Montreal Canadiens goaltender joked over the weekend he wouldn't mind trying one of the interactive games — specifically featuring a netminder sporting very familiar equipment — that sits among the many tributes to the sport's rich history. "It's pretty special to be able to look around," Price said before adding with a smile: "I was hoping to get the chance to shoot on myself downstairs." The 39-year-old was once at the pinnacle of his craft. Now he's taken his place alongside the game's greats. Price was inducted into the Hall as part of the 2026 class alongside Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the player category Monday. Brian Burke was enshrined as a builder. "When I was a kid, I had a dream that I can vividly remember," Price, who sported the Canadiens' red, white and blue for all 15 of his NHL seasons, said during his speech in downtown Toronto. "I was walking down a red carpet, just like in the Bell Centre. As I was walking, I approached a mountain of a figure. The No. 5 pick at the 2005 draft, Price won the Hart Trophy as league MVP and the Vezina Trophy as its top goaltender in 2015. The Anahim Lake, B.C., product finished with a 361-261-79 record, .917 save percentage, 2.51 goals-against average and 49 shutouts across 712 regular-season games in a career cut short by injury. Price had even better numbers in high-pressure moments before a knee issue ended his playing days beyond the 2021-22 campaign. He owned a .919 save percentage, 2.39 GAA and eight shutouts in 92 playoff contests, with his final post-season at the top of the list — willing the underdog Canadiens on an improbable push to the 2021 Stanley Cup final. items.title: Mammoth Recall Zac Jones
items.summary: The Utah Mammoth have recalled defenseman Zac Jones from AHL Tucson.
items.body: Register Login Mammoth Recall Zac Jones By Brian La Rose | at November 9, 2026 9:00 pm After returning Gregor Biber to AHL Tucson before he had a chance to play a game, it seemed likely that the Mammoth would be bringing someone else up to serve as a reserve option. They’ve now done just that, announcing ( Twitter link ) that they’ve recalled blueliner Zac Jones from Tucson. The 26-year-old is in his first season with Utah after inking a two-year, two-way contract following a non-tender by Buffalo back in June. Jones cleared waivers in training camp and has been with the Roadrunners since then. He’s off to a hot start as well, notching 11 points in 13 games to start the year. While Jones hasn’t seen any NHL action this season, he has a fair bit of experience at the top level. He has 115 games under his belt, all coming over parts of five seasons with the Rangers, who drafted him in the third round back in 2019. Jones has four goals and 24 assists in those outings in a little under 16 minutes per night of playing time. Even with Nate Schmidt out day-to-day, there’s no guarantee that Jones will see any ice time while on recall. He could just wind up being the seventh defender which would enable Artem Duda to remain in the lineup. Alternatively, if they want a bit more offensive upside on the back end, they could try Jones on the third pairing in the coming days.

Pittsburgh is 6-10-2 to start the year and sits at the bottom of the Eastern Conference, with little indication they will climb out of their poor start. The Penguins aren’t a quick team; they don’t play well defensively and lack toughness. They are also quite old by NHL standards, which is likely why they appear ready to start moving some of the older Penguins. Pittsburgh has several pending veteran UFAs, but two players remain useful and have another year on their deals. Those two players are Rickard Rakell and Bryan Rust , two veteran wingers who have been available via trade for over a year now and likely had suitors in the past. Now, with Pittsburgh in the spot it is in and those players another year older, it’s fair to wonder whether Pittsburgh will get the same kind of trade offers for those two men that they would have received in years past. In fairness to Pittsburgh, they will likely receive lower offers for any player they put on the market right now, simply because the entire team is struggling. Selling low generally brings out lower trade offers, as the NHL has always been a “What have you done for me lately” league. But even with Rust injured and Rakell inconsistent, they still have some trade value, and this’s probably the Penguins’ last chance to get anything significant for either player. items.body: Register Login Capitals Recall Justin Holl By Brennan McClain | at November 9, 2026 5:00 pm The Washington Capitals had a roster spot to fill after losing netminder Rémi Poirier off waivers earlier this afternoon. Washington quickly filled it, announcing they recalled defenseman Justin Holl from the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Holl, 34, earns his second call-up of the 2026-27 season. The Capitals signed Holl to a one-year, $900K contract this past offseason and recalled him earlier this season after Washington’s defensive corps suffered a few injuries. He looked good in his debut with Washington, scoring two goals in three games with a +1 rating, while averaging 12:59 of ice time per game. It’s a solid change of pace for Holl after the 10-year blueliner suffered through the worst stretch of his professional career with the Detroit Red Wings. Ahead of the 2023-24 season, the Red Wings signed Holl to a three-year, $10.2MM ($3.4MM AAV) contract after he spent the previous six years with the Toronto Maple Leafs. It started poorly, as Holl finished with only five assists in 38 games in his first season. Holl struggled again during the 2024-25 season, prompting Detroit to demote him. Last campaign, the final season of his three-year pact, Holl played exclusively for the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL before he was traded to the St. Louis Blues as a salary offset for the Justin Faulk trade. In fairness to Holl, he was never known as an offensive threat, but his production in Detroit was far lower than he was accustomed to in Toronto. Still, he also began to struggle defensively, producing a career-worst takeaway-to-turnover ratio in the 2024-25 season. Regardless, he has appeared far more comfortable in his limited action with the Capitals.

When the Jets host Hellebuyck and the New Jersey Devils at Canada Life Centre on Tuesday (7 p.m. ET; TSN3, MSGSN), Jake Allen will be in the visitor’s net with Hellebuyck as the backup . items.summary: Sheehan was a member of the Montreal Canadiens’ 1971 Stanley Cup championship team.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The hockey world has lost a member of the Montreal Canadiens ‘ 1971 Stanley Cup championship team. On Monday, the NHL Alumni Association announced that former center Bobby Sheehan passed away at the age of 77. The Weymouth, Massachusetts native was selected by the Canadiens out of the Ontario Hockey Association’s St. Catherines Black Hawks in the 1969 NHL Amateur Draft. He spent his first two professional seasons in Montreal’s organization, playing 45 total regular season games with the Canadiens and winning the Stanley Cup with Montreal in 1971. Sheehan joined the California Golden Seals for the 1971-72 season, where he scored 20 goals and added 26 assists for 46 points in 78 games. Following his lone season with the Golden Seals, Sheehan had a three-year stint in the World Hockey Association (WHA). His 1972-73 season with the WHA’s New York Raiders was the best of his career, putting up 35 goals and 53 assists for 88 points in 75 games. He stayed with New York (which would be renamed the New York Golden Blades and then the Jersey Knights) for most of the 1973-74 season before moving on to the Edmonton Oilers through the 1974-75 season. Sheehan returned to the NHL with the Chicago Black Hawks in the 1975-76 season, and then played for the Detroit Red Wings in the 1976-77 season. He went back to the WHA for one last season in 1977-78, when played for the Indianapolis Racers. Sheehan then spent the rest of his career splitting time between the New York Rangers , Colorado Rockies, and Los Angeles Kings of the NHL, the New Haven Nighthawks and Binghamton Whalers of the American Hockey League (AHL), and the Forth Worth Texans of the Central Hockey League (CHL), before retiring in 1983. When speaking to the media, Columbus Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness announced that forward Conor Garland will not be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Blue Jackets take on the Florida Panthers . Bowness said Garland is battling back from an upper-body injury but didn’t provide a timeline for his return. It isn’t quite clear when or where Garland was hurt. He played the entirety of Columbus’ last contest, a 5-2 loss to the Buffalo Sabres this past Friday night. The 30-year-old was a -2 while logging a little over 13 minutes of ice time, not too far from his average for the year. Garland had appeared in each of the Jackets’ first 15 games of the 2026-27 season, but has definitely looked far from the offensive threat he was earlier in his career. He has just one assist to his name to go along with his plus/minus of -5 while averaging 13:33 of ice time per game. This is the Scituate, Mass. native’s first full season in Columbus. He was traded to the Blue Jackets ahead of last year’s trade deadline from the Vancouver Canucks , as he was expected to provide an offensive boost as they battled to stay in the Wild Card race. He scored five goals and seven points in the remaining 21 games, but the Jackets came short of clinching a playoff berth. With Garland out, expect to see Ryan Lomberg back in the lineup, joining Steven Lorentz and Jack Williams on the fourth line during practice on Monday. The Blue Jackets (7-8-0) sit sixth in the Metropolitan Division, six points back of the last Wild Card position in the Eastern Conference.

We are now 41 days into the fantasy season and are witnessing teams start to separate in our league standings. It’s a long season, but we are nearing the quarter-mark. Here’s what we learned in Week 6 of fantasy hockey as we try not to overreact while we question what is happening with our goaltenders right now. Gauthier scored in every game during Week 6, extending his historic goal streak to six games with his 13th goal and 44th shot during that stretch. It is the most goals ever during a six-game span, leaving fantasy owners to wonder if they have a potential 70-goal scorer on their hands. The 22-year-old has really turned it on after a slow start to the 2026-27 campaign, where he potted just two goals in his first 11 games. He is now on pace for a whopping 70 goals and 336 SOG across the full 84-game season after missing one game earlier this year. He also led all skaters with three game-winning goals last week, single-handedly dominating that category. Across the last seven days, a surprising seven teams went undefeated as New Jersey (4), Anaheim (4), Nashville (3), Boston (3), New York Rangers (3), Winnipeg (3) and Ottawa (2) all went without a loss. On the other side of the coin, four teams failed to pick up a win as Chicago (4), San Jose (4), Vancouver (3) and Toronto (3) went without a win in Week 6. With both Michael Misa and Gabriel Perreault joining both their teams’ top power-play unit and top line this past week, we are watching more teams lacking offence turn to their young upcoming superstars for immediate solutions.

items.body: BROSSARD, Que. — There was a sequence in last Tuesday’s game against the Winnipeg Jets that was perfectly indicative of Arber Xhekaj ’s improvement this season, and it came long before he threw his last right-hand cross at Tyrel Bauer’s head. It was in the ninth minute of the second period when Xhekaj set up a great one-timer opportunity in the offensive zone for Adam Engstrom and then hustled back into position in his own end to simultaneously deny a zone entry and a hit from Viggo Bjorck. In both instances, Xhekaj steadied himself, chose the play he was going to make before the puck arrived, and executed to perfection. The pass to Engstrom was the best of several decisions Xhekaj could’ve made in that situation, and it led to a quality scoring chance. And everything he did immediately after that led to the Canadiens continuing one of their only good sequences of the game — and led Bjorck back to the Jets’ bench worse for wear after bearing the brunt of a collision he initiated. That had to feel good for Xhekaj, who was one of roughly five Canadiens who didn’t need a hard look in the mirror after that history-making loss. He was as effective in that game as he had been in each of the 13 games he’d appeared in before it this season, and he’s been just as good since, providing more evidence of just how comfortable he’s become in the role he had so much trouble nailing down last season. items.summary: The Swedish-born American set unique history and ranks third in the NHL with 15 goals through 17 games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Anaheim Ducks forward Cutter Gauthier is enjoying himself this season and making history as the Ducks establish themselves as one of the NHL’s most thrilling teams through the first quarter of the 2026-27 regular season. On Sunday night, with a three-goal, one-assist performance in a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins , he became the first player in NHL history to score three hat tricks within the first 10 days of a calendar month. Gauthier leaned on an empty-net goal in the final minute to earn himself the historic honor, as the Ducks became the first team since the 1988-90 LA Kings to score at least five goals in eight consecutive games. The 22-year-old started the month in peak form, scoring his first November hat trick on Nov. 1 in a 6-3 win over the Ottawa Senators . Two days later, he potted another trio against the struggling Vancouver Canucks in a 5-4 victory. Both of his first two hat-tricks in November included two power-play goals, as he makes the most of Anaheim’s league-leading 38.5 percent success rate on the man advantage this season. Yet, his history-making performance against the Penguins didn’t need any special-teams help, with two goals coming at five-on-five before he netted the empty-net marker to seal the victory. Through 17 games this season, the Swedish-born American has 15 goals, good for third in the NHL, and seven assists for 22 points, ranking him 17th in NHL scoring overall. In his career, he has 76 goals and 60 assists for 136 points in 176 games with the Ducks and, previously, the Philadelphia Flyers . After Sunday’s win, the Ducks sit third in the Pacific Division with 21 points through the first 18 games of the 84-game campaign, as they look ahead to a Wednesday night home game against the Nashville Predators.

Wading through a difficult stretch of injuries that’s already seen pivotal contributors Kirill Marchenko and Morgan Rielly pulled from the lineup, the blue-and-white took the ice Sunday night hoping to find some redemption in the wake of a disappointing loss to the Montreal Canadiens 24 hours earlier. Then came the news that top-line winger Jack Roslovic, who’s been working through a nagging injury all week, was unable to go. The quick-footed winger took warmups with the team, believing he’d be able to suit up for his club’s meeting with the New Jersey Devils, wanting to contribute. Danna Ramadan couldn’t imagine going to a college without being able to play hockey. “I’ve been around hockey my entire life,” said Ramadan, a 19-year-old goalie from Somerset, New Jersey. “There really was no world where I wouldn't be playing hockey in college. items.body: WINNIPEG — Brayden Yager was grinning ear to ear while surrounded by reporters following a roller-coaster Sunday night at Canada Life Centre. The 21-year-old Winnipeg forward had just notched his first NHL goal — which was also his first NHL point — to help lift the Jets to an eventful 4-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning. What made the milestone extra special was the small family cheering section sitting rinkside that shared in the meaningful moment. “Mom, dad and grandpa were here, so it was pretty cool to do it in front of them," Yager said after the game, still dripping with sweat. "Unbelievable feeling. Dream come true.” The Saskatchewan native's memorable moment was born out of a bloody sequence early in the third period. Winnipeg (7-8-3) was already protecting a 2-0 lead on second-period goals from Cole Perfetti and Morgan Barron when Lightning forward Pontus Holmberg caught Yager in the mouth with a high stick. The infraction drew blood, resulting in a four-minute double-minor penalty and a quick check-in with the team's medical staff. Yager was back on the ice moments later. With nine seconds remaining in the first minor, he fired a one-timer past Tampa Bay goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy after a slick deflected feed from fellow rookie Viggo Bjorck. "Just a great play by Viggo there that touched over to me and I had a pretty wide-open net," Yager said. "You can definitely feel it, the atmosphere. I thought the fans were unbelievable tonight." Bjorck, selected eighth overall by Winnipeg in June's draft, collected his third assist in two games after enduring a 16-game scoring drought to begin his rookie campaign. items.summary: It isn’t quite clear what led to Sissons not returning to Sunday’s game against the Devils.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Another injury blow to the blue and white. When the third period between the Toronto Maple Leafs and New Jersey Devil s began on Sunday night, the Maple Leafs announced that forward Colton Sissons wouldn’t be returning to the game due to a lower-body injury. It isn’t quite clear what exactly led to Sissons exiting the contest. The 33-year-old logged just 9:55 of ice time, which ended up being the second-fewest minutes among Leaf skaters. He registered a plus/minus of -1, as Toronto fell to the Devils by a final score of 4-0. If Sissons is forced to miss time, he joins a list of notable Leafs who have missed considerable time. Chris Tanev, Morgan Rielly, and Nick Blankenburg are a trio of defensemen who are on the shelf, with Kirill Marchenko and Jack Roslovic also in the press box. Sissons signed a two-year contract with the Leafs this past summer, with the deal carrying an AAV of $4.25 million. He was brought in to provide needed depth down the middle for a Leafs team that was looking to bounce back after a disappointing 2025-26 campaign. In appearing in each of the team’s first 19 contests, Sissons has scored two goals and four assists for six points, with an even plus/minus, averaging less than 15 minutes of ice time per game. He picked up an assist in the Leafs’ 4-2 loss to the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday, but hasn’t found the back of the net since Oct. 17 against the New York Islanders . items.title: Scheifele’s winner with 1.6 seconds remaining lifts Jets over Lightning
items.body: Mark Scheifele scored with 1.6 seconds remaining in the third period to lead the Winnipeg Jets to a 4-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Sunday. With the period winding down and the Jets on a 5-on-3 power play, Scheifele converted a pass from Cole Perfetti before firing home a slapshot to seal the win at Canada Life Centre. "(Perfetti) and Gabe (Vilardi) getting dirty in the corner and making a great play," Scheifele said of his goal after the win. "That was an unbelievable pass and you don't quit until the buzzer, and that was exactly that." Scheifele said that he "had no idea" how much time was left on the clock when he secured the pass from Perfetti, but added that he "wasn't going to waste (his) time looking at the clock" when the puck came out. Tampa Bay tied the game 3-3 with a pair of Pontus Holmberg goals 26 seconds apart late in the third period. "It's not very fun," Scheifele said of the swing on the scoreboard. "It's definitely not how we wanted to win that game, but kudos to them. ... That's a good hockey team right there. They don't quit. Even on a back-to-back, being down three, they kept making plays, they kept doing good things. Morgan Barron, Brayden Yager and Perfetti also scored for Winnipeg (7-8-3), which extended its win streak to three games after dropping its previous nine. Rookie Viggo Bjorck tallied two assists. Yager's tally marked his first NHL goal in his sixth game with the Jets. "That was really cool," the 21-year-old said post-game. items.title: Kings Assign Martin Chromiak To AHL
items.summary: The Los Angeles Kings have assigned winger Martin Chromiak to AHL Ontario.
items.body: Register Login Kings Assign Martin Chromiak To AHL By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 8:26 pm With the Kings activating Alex Turcotte off injured reserve yesterday, winger Martin Chromiak found himself out of the lineup. Now, he’s off the roster altogether, as the team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve returned Chromiak to AHL Ontario. The 24-year-old was brought up about a week and a half ago but didn’t see much action, getting into just two games. That said, they were Chromiak’s first two appearances at the NHL level. He was held off the scoresheet while recording three shots on goal and two hits in a little over 13 minutes per night of ice time. A 2020 fifth-round pick, Chromiak had gotten off to a hot start with the Reign to earn this short-lived promotion. Prior to the recall, he had collected six goals and two assists in nine games. He basically picked up where he left off a year ago, when he had 28 goals and 28 assists in 71 outings with Ontario, a performance that earned him a one-year, two-way deal worth $850K in the NHL and $200K in guaranteed money this offseason. With the Kings operating very tight to the cap ceiling this season, Chromiak’s assignment now gives them enough cap space to be able to bring someone up should more injuries arise. In the meantime, they now have one open roster spot, with veterans Mats Zuccarello and Kevin Fiala working their way towards a return to the lineup. Accordingly, one more spot will need to be opened up when both wingers are able to return.

items.summary: The Florida Panthers have recalled winger Jack Devine from AHL Charlotte.
items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Jack Devine By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 6:46 pm Prior to their game against Boston this afternoon, the Panthers added some extra depth to their forward group. The team announced that they’ve recalled winger Jack Devine from AHL Charlotte. The 23-year-old was a seventh-round pick back in 2021, going 221st overall in 2022 and has clearly outperformed that draft selection. After a strong four seasons at the University of Denver (including tallying 56 and 57 points in his final two years), Devine turned pro last season, playing predominantly with the Checkers. In 63 games with them in 2025-26, Devine had a good rookie campaign, tallying 18 goals and 25 assists. He had a brief two-week stint with Florida early on in the year, getting into six games with the Panthers although he was held off the scoresheet. This season, Devine got off to an impressive start with Charlotte, notching nine goals and three assists through 11 appearances. Devine’s recall comes on the heels of the injury that Sandis Vilmanis sustained on Saturday. Head coach Paul Maurice indicated that while they’ve had a doctor look at the youngster already, they probably won’t get a full assessment of the injury until they return home. Florida has one game left on its road trip on Tuesday in Columbus so it will be a few more days before the severity of the injury to Vilmanis is known. In the short term, Devine will serve as the extra forward while they get a better sense of how long Vilmanis will be out for. Depending on the severity of the injury, Florida could reassess who they want in the reserve role from there. The Panthers had an open roster spot so no corresponding move needed to be made to bring Devine up.

Kicking off Year 12 for the undrafted veteran, Gourde is back on the second line alongside Anthony Cirelli and Brandon Hagel . The 34-year-old underwent hip surgery over the summer, and back in September it was thought he’d be out until December, returning considerably sooner than expected. Going from an ECHLer to a two-time Stanley Cup champion and legitimate top-six threat, Gourde returned to Tampa after 3 1/2 years with the Kraken. A beloved veteran no longer expected to drive the same amount of offense, he suited up for all 82 games last year recording 28 points. It was the fourth time the spark plug surpassed the 100-hit mark, landing 115. Facing multiple first round playoff exits, the Lightning made an effort to strengthen their middle-six along with adding a star in John Carlson . Their current 11-3-2 record speaks to the improvements made during the offseason. items.title: Report: Blackhawks not making coaching change amid slump
items.body: It appears the Chicago Blackhawks are staying the course amid some choppy waters. Jeff Blashill will remain as Blackhawks' head coach as the team has opted not to make a coaching change, The Athletic 's Scott Powers reported on Sunday. The Blackhawks, in a rebuild for the better part of a decade, were intending this to be a season in which they turned a corner. Instead, they've started the year 4-13-1 — better only than the lowly Vancouver Canucks in the Western Conference. Things hit a low point with a 9-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night. The Blackhawks were off Sunday and don't play again until Thursday, which led many to wonder whether regime change is imminent. Instead, it appears general manager Kyle Davidson is giving Blashill some more time to right the ship. The former Detroit Red Wings coach was hired by Chicago ahead of the 2025-26 season. The Blackhawks missed the playoffs for the sixth consecutive season with a 29-39-14 record.

items.title: Hertl scores pair, Golden Knights beat Sabres for third win in a row
items.body: BUFFALO, N.Y. — Tomas Hertl scored two goals and the Vegas Golden Knights won their third straight game, 4-1 over the Buffalo Sabres on Sunday. Hertl scored both of his goals in the third period to help put the game away for the Golden Knights, who finished their road trip 3-0-1. Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner also scored for Vegas while Adin Hill made 27 saves. Beck Malenstyn scored and Colten Ellis made 21 saves for Buffalo, which has lost two of its last three games. Marner opened the scoring with a short-handed goal at 12:17 of the second period following a turnover by Tage Thompson. Eichel, who was the Sabres' first-round draft pick in 2015 and traded to Vegas in 2021, made it 2-0 one minute and 26 seconds later with his eighth goal of the season. He has seven goals and three assists in eight games against Buffalo in his career. Malenstyn cut the Vegas lead to 2-1 with his first goal on a goalmouth scrum at 4:26 of the third period, but Hertl made it 3-1 just 1:17 later. Hertl’s second of the game and ninth of the season made it 4-1 at 10:00. Buffalo concludes a four-game homestand against Tampa Bay on Wednesday night. Vegas begins a five-game homestand against Utah on Wednesday night.

items.summary: Arvid Soderblom looks to be getting sent back to the AHL after a tough start to the season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images A couple of netminders have hit the wire. On Sunday, the Chicago Blackhawks placed goaltender Arvid Soderblom on waivers, with the Washington Capitals doing the same with fellow backstop Remi Poirier. Soderblom entered the 2026-27 season set to be the backup to Spencer Knight once again. However, while the Blackhawks have struggled as a whole, Soderblom’s play has been anything but up to par. In five appearances so far, four starts, the 27-year-old has allowed 21 goals, giving him a 4.67 goals-against average and a .842 save percentage, along with a 0-3-1 record. Who the Hawks would call up to take his place is yet to be determined. Drew Commesso has been with the organization the longest, having played a couple of games with Chicago on top of his time with the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs, but Stanislav Berezhnoy has had better numbers early on this year with Rockford. In 117 NHL games, Soderblom has a record of 25-68-15, with a 3.65 GAA, a .885 SV% and one shutout. He’s in the final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in July 2025. The deal carries an AAV of $2.75 million. Poirier was acquired by the Capitals last Sunday in exchange for a seventh-round pick from the New Jersey Devils , as the Devils had to make some roster moves after receiving Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets . Poirier, who was claimed off waivers by the Devils from the Dallas Stars , has yet to play a game this season. He has spent the past three seasons with the Stars’ top farm team, the Texas Stars. In 137 regular-season games in the AHL, the 25-year-old is 70-51-16, with a 2.76 GAA, a .908 SV% and six shutouts. He’s also 11-9 in 23 Calder Cup Playoff contests, with a 2.42 GAA, a .909 SV% and three shutouts.

items.body: Defenseman skating again after sustaining skull fracture during preseason game ST. PAUL, Minn. -- Brock Faber practiced with the Minnesota Wild for the second straight day on Friday, and the defenseman understands the fractured skull he sustained during a preseason game "could have been a lot worse." Faber returned to the ice this week after recovering from a skull fracture he sustained during a preseason game against the Dallas Stars on Sept. 25, when he was hit in the head with a shot during the second period. The puck hit him around the ear area that isn't protected by the helmet. "It could have been a lot worse if, one, if I got hit harder in that spot, and two, if I didn’t get the medical attention that I did," he said. "I'm so glad to just put it in the past. It's so good to be back. "If it would have got me a couple centimeters lower, it just would have hit me in the ear and I'd had to maybe get a couple stitches on my ear. If it would have hit me a couple inches or centimeters higher, it hits me in the helmet and I'm fine. The area where I got hit, only a puck could fit there. items.summary: The Washington Capitals’ Tom Wilson won’t face further discipline after his actions on Saturday night.
items.body: The Washington Capitals ' Tom Wilson won't face further discipline after his actions on Saturday. Wilson delivered a hard hit to the back of Florida Panthers ' Sandis Vilmanis in the first period that sent the forward headfirst into the area where the glass meets the boards. Vilmanis left the game and did not return, and Wilson received a major penalty for boarding and a game misconduct for the play. After speculation about whether Wilson would face a hearing for the hit, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Sunday that he's hearing the Capitals' star will not face supplemental discipline. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said after the game that Florida was waiting on more information about Vilmanis' condition. “Getting looked at by another doctor tomorrow," he said. "But probably we’ll have to wait until we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, get some imaging.” Wilson has been suspended several times during his 14-year career. He was given 20 games for a blindside hit to the head in 2018, a ban later reduced to 14 games on appeal after he had already served 16. He received a seven-game suspension for boarding Boston’s Brandon Carlo with head contact in 2021 and six games in 2024 for a stick to the face of Toronto Maple Leafs forward Noah Gregor. The 22-year-old Vilmanis had his first career two-goal game Wednesday night when Florida beat Chicago.

This update will return Russia to the top flight of international hockey after serving a six-year suspension from the IIHF. Russia and Belarus were banned from international hockey following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2021.
